name: Zen Center Athens
tradition: Soto Zen Buddhism, in the lineage of Hosshin-ji monastery (Sekkei Harada / Koten Roshi)
technique: Zazen (seated meditation); kinhin (walking meditation); oryoki formal meal practice; sesshin liturgy (chanting, prostrations, dokusan) in the Soto Zen tradition of Dogen
teacherAccess: Dharma talks, ceremony leadership and periodic dokusan (private interviews) with Koten Roshi during his roughly twice-yearly visits from Japan; day-to-day practice is guided by Dharma-transmitted teacher Konstantinos Sgoumpopoulos and other visiting Zen teachers
retreatOptions: Multi-day sesshins (5 days / 4 nights) held two to three times a year at Kaisanji on the island of Serifos, aimed at experienced zazen practitioners rather than complete beginners; separate weekend zazen days and yoga-inflected retreats are also offered through the Athens dojo
about: Zen Center Athens is a Soto Zen sangha founded in 2013 by Konstantinos Sgoumpopoulos after he trained under and received Dharma transmission from Koten Roshi, a senior monk (Godo Roshi) of Hosshin-ji monastery in Fukui, Japan, in a lineage connected to Sekkei Harada and Shunryu Suzuki Roshi. Alongside its city dojo in Athens (Saikenji), the center is developing Kaisanji - 'the temple of the mountain and the sea' - a Zen monastery on a remote stretch of coast near Kalo Ampeli beach on the island of Serifos, where it holds multi-day sesshins several times a year. Kaisanji sesshins follow Hosshinji's monastic program: practice is done in silence without phones, computers or books, meals are taken in the traditional oryoki style, and days run from a 4am wake-up bell through a full schedule of zazen, chanting, work practice (samu) and dokusan interviews, with lights out at 9:30pm. Koten Roshi travels from Japan roughly twice a year to lead sesshins and give personal instruction, and the center has also hosted visiting teachers connected to the San Francisco Zen Center, including Shohaku Okumura. The 5-day sesshins include on-site meals and simple monastic-style accommodation in cells built for monks and visitors, and are intended for practitioners with some prior zazen experience.
schedule: Sesshin daily schedule runs from a 4am wake-up bell through alternating periods of zazen, kinhin, morning and evening liturgy, oryoki meals, work practice (samu) and evening zazen, with lights out at 9:30pm; regular zazen and one-day sittings continue at the Athens dojo between Kaisanji retreats
cost: 5-day Kaisanji sesshin: EUR 250, or EUR 350 for the session led in person by Koten Roshi, covering meals and accommodation for the retreat; ferry travel to Serifos is extra

pricePerDay.notes: 5-night sesshin: EUR 250 regular fee or EUR 350 for the sesshin with Koten Roshi present, both covering meals and accommodation, divided across 5 nights.

foodNotes: Meals during sesshin are taken in the traditional monastic oryoki style and are included in the retreat fee; specific dietary style (vegetarian/vegan/other) is not stated online.
workNotes: The daily sesshin schedule includes a work period (samu) as part of standard monastic practice.
